To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Lsh mediated transcriptional silencing at HoxC genes is associated with Pol II stalling; 2) Pol II stalling is dependent on DNA methylation and catalytically active Dnmt; 3) Lsh mediated Pol II stalling involves the chromodomain helicase protein Chd1; and 4) Lsh mediated Hox gene silencing is dependent on Pol II stalling and independent of histone H3K9 trimethylation
Lsh-mediated Pol II stalling at methylated Hoc genes is dependent on the presence of catalytically active DNMT1 and that Chd1 mediates transcriptional elongation in the absence of Lsh.
DNA methylation is compatible with Pol II stalling and that Lsh mediated RNA Pol II stalling involves DNA methylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the epigenetics factor Lsh in transcriptional regulation of Hox genes.
the epigenetic regulation of transcriptional silencing at Hox genes.
the molecular mechanisms of gene regulation in dependence of epigenetic mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Lsh-mediated Pol II stalling at Hox genes involves DNA methylation.
Lsh mediated DNA methylation at Hox genes leads to a nucleosome free region and transcriptional silencing via Pol-II stalling.
DNA methylation and histone modifications are not mutually exclusive and that both are compatible with Pol II recruitment and Pol II staling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA methylation at Hox genes is compatible with transcriptional elongation, however, Pol II stalling at Hox genes requires DNA methylation and the epigenetic modifier Lsh.
the epigenetic modifier Lsh is a negative regulator of Hox genes and acts in concert with DNA methylation to repress Hox gene expression.
Lsh mediated Pol II stalling at Hox genes is associated with CpG methylation and is dependent on the catalytic activity of DNA methylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA methylation at Hox genes is compatible with Pol II stalling, but the molecular mechanism of this repression involves the epigenetic modulator Lsh.
DNA methylation and Lsh are required to mediate Pol II stalling, which is an important regulatory mechanism to silence developmentally important genes.
DNA methylation and Pol II stabling are compatible at selected genes and the mechanism by which Pol II stalling acts as a repressive mechanism is described.
